Nova Ushytsya Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Khmelnytskyi Oblast, Ukraine

Not demolished. In the late 18th century, Nova Ushytsya hosted congresses of Admorim — gatherings of Hasidic rebbes. In 1838, 82 Jews of the town and its outskirts were arrested on suspicion of falsifying census data; most were tortured, and 30 died from it, in what became known as the Novoushitsky case. Israel Friedman (1796–1850), head of the Ruzhin Hasidic dynasty documented at length elsewhere in this collection, was also arrested in this case but released for lack of evidence — though this account differs somewhat from the record documented at Ruzhyn itself, which describes his 1838 arrest as connected to the murder of two Jewish informers and states he was held for two years before release; this discrepancy is flagged here rather than resolved. In 1913, local Zionists and Bundists protested the Beilis case, the internationally notorious blood libel trial in Kyiv. Mendel Daychman organized a self-defense detachment in 1918. In August 1942, 3,222 Jews were murdered, and some were deported to the Letychiv ghetto, documented elsewhere in this collection.
